status_values.columns_consistent_with_form: the recorded columns of tests.csv agree with each other in the way the card's form or range says, by the card's criterion; this is not an independent test of a physical law

cards.title: Olson and Ferkul 2012, Eq. 1 oxygen margin by gravity level, recomputed from their Table I

check.description: For every material row of OF2012.table1, recompute Eq. 1 for the three low-gravity levels from the four limits of that row and compare with the printed margin. Then compare the smallest printed margin per level over the three materials with the values of OF2012.margin.

criterion.text: matches_published_table if every recomputed value differs from the printed value by at most half a unit of the printed value's last decimal, and every smallest printed margin equals the value of OF2012.margin; otherwise differs_from_published_table.

result.computation_label: team arithmetic on values of the reference items

caption.means: The printed margins of Table I follow from the printed limits by Eq. 1 as the paper states it. Team arithmetic on published values.
caption.does_not_mean: It does not check the limits themselves. Each material was tested at one pressure, so the margins say nothing about another pressure. The low-gravity limits come from 5.18 s drop-tower tests whose criteria differ from the 1g criteria. The paper's Conclusions give 5.75 for Martian gravity while Table I gives it for Lunar; the card uses the table.

cards.title: d-squared form of droplet burning, checked as a relation between recorded FLEX columns
cards.not_in_our_references_note: No item of references.json states the d-squared form (d^2 = d0^2 - K t). The team wrote it from general knowledge of combustion. TP216046.columns is held only as the pointer to the column definitions of the FLEX table and does not state the form. The script searches every item for the words listed under 'absence_search' and stops if one is found.

check.description: For every FLEX row with an initial diameter, an extinction diameter above zero and below the initial one, a burning rate above zero and a burn time above zero, compute burn_time_s / ((d0^2 - d_ext^2) / K) (team computation; K read as mm2/s, as the team reads the column) and describe its distribution (count, minimum, quartiles and median by NIST e-Handbook 7.2.6.2, method R6, maximum), overall and per fuel and test end. No criterion: the held K is fitted from shortly after ignition to extinction (NASA/TP-2015-216046 Appendix, not yet an item of references.json) and d0 is the diameter when the igniters are turned on, so the ratio is not a test of any law.

result.filter: source_id == 'flex' and initial_diameter_mm > 0 and extinction_diameter_mm > 0 and extinction_diameter_mm < initial_diameter_mm and burning_rate_mm2_s > 0 and burn_time_s > 0
result.quantile_method: NIST e-Handbook 7.2.6.2 percentiles (method R6 of Hyndman and Fan): position p(N+1) in the ordered values, linear between neighbours, ends clamped
result.removed: criterion (median band, share band, minimum share), bands and the reversal placebo: chosen after the numbers were seen; no held or opened source defines them (model map L12, M07)

caption.means: The distribution of a team ratio over recorded FLEX columns. Team computation, not a NASA conclusion.
caption.does_not_mean: This is not a test of a physical law and gives no agreement status: K is itself a reported value of the same experiment, fitted over part of the burn, and the form is not stated by any document we hold. No threshold is applied.
